title: Production incident: encryption enabled without keystore provisioning
notes: Incident response session: symptom, root cause, rollback, follow-up fixes.

turns.text: Production is throwing 500s on /ingest/transcript since the last deploy 10 minutes ago. Can you check?

Checking the logs... the new build enabled security.encryption.enabled: true by default, but the deploy script didn't provision an OS keystore entry on this box, so DB open is failing with a keystore error on every request.
Rolled back to the previous release tag v0.7.3. 500s stopped within 30 seconds of rollback completing.
Once it's stable, what's the actual fix so we can redeploy the new version safely?
The deploy script needs a pre-flight step that provisions the keystore entry BEFORE flipping encryption.enabled to true, not after. I'll add that as a required step in the deploy runbook.
Do that, and add a doctor check that catches this before it ever reaches prod again.
Added a doctor check: if security.encryption.enabled is true but no keystore entry exists, doctor now fails loudly instead of the daemon crashing on first real request.

gold_atoms.text: Production incident: /ingest/transcript started returning 500s about 10 minutes after a deploy that enabled security.encryption.enabled by default without provisioning the OS keystore entry first.
Flipping encryption.enabled to true before the deploy script provisions the OS keystore entry causes DB-open failures on every request in production.
Rolled back production to release tag v0.7.3 to stop the 500s; 500s stopped within 30 seconds of rollback.
The deploy runbook must provision the keystore entry BEFORE flipping encryption.enabled to true, as a required pre-flight step.
Added a doctor check that fails loudly if encryption.enabled is true but no keystore entry exists, instead of the daemon crashing on first real request.
